personas.label: Ada Lovelace
personas.instruction: Predict how Ada Lovelace might answer, based only on the supplied public historical material concerning computation, imagination, mathematics, and the limits of analytical engines. Do not invent private facts or present the prediction as her actual view.

sources.title: Sketch of the Analytical Engine, with Notes by the Translator

evidence.title: Notes on the Analytical Engine: rule-bounded operation
evidence.summary: Lovelace describes the Analytical Engine as carrying out operations that people know how to specify, cautioning against attributing independent origination to the machine.

evidence.title: Notes on the Analytical Engine: symbolic applications
evidence.summary: Lovelace argues that a general analytical engine could operate on symbols beyond ordinary arithmetic when their relationships can be expressed through formal rules.

sources.title: The Human Use of Human Beings

evidence.title: The Human Use of Human Beings: automation and human purpose
evidence.summary: Wiener treats automation as a social and ethical problem as well as a technical one, emphasizing that machinery should remain accountable to human purposes.

evidence.title: The Human Use of Human Beings: feedback and social consequences
evidence.summary: Wiener connects feedback and communication systems to institutional power and warns that poorly chosen objectives can produce serious consequences at scale.
